replies.user: [CURRICULUM: Unit 1, Lesson 1] Teach me what physically happens inside an LLM when I type a prompt. Start with tokenization and next-token prediction. After explaining, give me a hands-on exercise.
replies.raw:
Here's something that might surprise you: the word "bank" is technically the same token whether you're talking about a river or a place to store money.

That means the model starts with *zero* idea which one you mean — and has to figure it out from context. That's the whole puzzle this lesson is about.

**Tokenization** is step one. Before an LLM reads a single word, it chops your text into chunks called tokens. A token is usually a common word or a word-fragment.

"Running" might stay as one token; "unbelievable" might split into two or three.

Each token gets converted to a number — a token ID — so the model works with math, not letters.

[EX]GPT-4's tokenizer has a vocabulary of roughly 100,000 tokens. A short sentence like "The cat sat on the mat" might become 7 tokens; a rare technical word might take 4 or 5 tokens all by itself.[/EX]

[KEY]Tokenization turns your words into numbers before the model sees anything.[/KEY]

[Q]
What is a token in the context of an LLM?
A) A full sentence the model reads all at once
B) A chunk of text — often a word or word-fragment — converted to a number
C) A copy of the original prompt stored in the model's memory
ANS: B
[/Q]

**Tokenization** is the very first thing that happens when you hit send.

Your prompt doesn't enter the model as words — it gets chopped into chunks called tokens, which are then converted to numbers.

[EX]The word "playing" might become two tokens: "play" and "ing." A short common word like "the" is usually one token. A rare or technical word might get split into three or four pieces.[/EX]

[KEY]Before an LLM reads a single word of your prompt, it converts everything into numbered tokens — that's the only language the model actually speaks.[/KEY]

[Q]
What is a token in the context of an LLM?
A) A full sentence that the model reads all at once
B) A chunk of text (part of a word, a word, or punctuation) converted to a number
C) A copy of your prompt stored in the model's memory
ANS: B
[/Q]
